name: Industrials & Manufacturing
one_liner: Making machinery, equipment, components and automation systems for other businesses, where scale, operational excellence and aftermarket service drive returns.
how_it_makes_money: Manufacturers sell capital equipment and components to customers in construction, energy, autos and other industries, often through dealers or distributors. Aftermarket parts, service contracts and software recur over the equipment's life and usually carry higher margins than the original sale. Many firms run a portfolio of segments serving different end markets.
revenue_formula: Revenue = units sold × average selling price + installed base × aftermarket revenue per unit
Aftermarket revenue = installed base × attach rate × spend per unit per year
cost_structure: Materials and components: often the largest cost, e.g. steel and electronics
SG&A, including sales and dealer support
margins: Operating margins commonly range from mid single digits for commodity components to high teens or better for leaders with strong aftermarket businesses. Mix of aftermarket, pricing power, lean operations and cycle exposure drive the spread.

key_metrics.name: Book-to-bill ratio
key_metrics.what: Orders versus shipments; above 1 signals growing demand.

key_metrics.name: Backlog
key_metrics.what: Orders not yet delivered, giving revenue visibility.

key_metrics.name: Aftermarket share of revenue
key_metrics.what: Higher share means steadier, higher-margin revenue.

key_metrics.name: Capacity utilization
key_metrics.what: Drives fixed-cost absorption and unit cost.

key_metrics.name: Organic growth
key_metrics.what: Growth excluding M&A and currency, the key underlying signal.

key_metrics.name: Free cash flow conversion
key_metrics.what: Share of net income converted to cash; working capital heavy firms lag.

trends: Reshoring and nearshoring manufacturing to the US and Mexico
Tariffs and trade policy raising input costs and reshaping supply chains
Electrification and data center buildout boosting electrical equipment demand
Factory automation, robotics and industrial AI

case_angles.question: A machinery maker's margins are falling despite rising sales; why?
Should an industrial conglomerate break itself up?
Should a manufacturer move production from China to Mexico?
How can a manufacturer grow its aftermarket services business?

interview_hooks: Do conglomerates still make sense, or do focused companies create more value?
Will reshoring meaningfully bring manufacturing back to the US?
How much of an equipment maker's future value is in software and services?
